At this table, Maya set out to draw a fish: "nose on the left, forked tail on the right." Early on, the fish was "mostly up," but its body wasn't connected to the tail. She fixed the joint, added the top of the body, and kept checking the link by the tail.

As the warnings came from the facilitator, Maya kept working the same spot. "Body still isn't lighting up, checking the joint by the tail," she noted. She bridged the gap at the tail, then began retracing the lower body and fin so they would hook onto it.

In the end, none of the dominoes fell. Maya said her picture was a fish. The blind judges saw only a faint, nearly invisible drawing on a blank cream background.
